overview: Two ways animals move blood through their bodies — one lets blood freely bathe tissues, the other keeps blood confined to vessels.
genZNote: Open system: blood just floods the whole space and soaks everything. Closed system: blood stays strictly inside its pipes.

aspects.label: Blood Contained in Vessels?
aspects.valueA: No — blood (haemolymph) directly bathes tissues in open spaces called sinuses.
aspects.valueB: Yes — blood remains enclosed within vessels (arteries, veins, capillaries) at all times.

aspects.label: Blood Pressure
aspects.valueA: Lower blood pressure and slower circulation.
aspects.valueB: Higher blood pressure, allowing faster and more efficient circulation.

aspects.label: Efficiency for Active Animals
aspects.valueA: Less efficient — generally suits smaller or less active animals.
aspects.valueB: More efficient — supports larger, more metabolically active animals.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Insects rely on an open circulatory system, which is one reason their body size and activity level are physically limited.
overlay.memoryTrick: Open = haemolymph floods open spaces. Closed = blood stays sealed inside vessels.
overlay.commonMisconception: An open circulatory system does not mean the animal has no heart — insects and molluscs do have a simple pumping heart, blood just isn't confined to vessels after leaving it.
